A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ELSA/ELSA-L research and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. Relocated experiments and renumbered tables can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original pruning experiments, perplexity and zero-shot accuracy measurements, scalability results, and objective/projection ablations in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds extreme-sparsity comparisons, inference measurements, and pruning-cost results in Sections 5.2, 5.3, and 5.5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same sparsity-constrained objective, ADMM updates, Fisher-weighted projection, and ELSA-L quantization procedure. Appendix Algorithm 1 is also unchanged. The added MACKO benchmarking backend does not revise the proposed pruning algorithm.

E1.justification: C4, WikiText2, and the seven zero-shot tasks are retained. V2 adds an end-to-end text-generation deployment scenario in Section 5.3, beyond v1's perplexity and task-accuracy evaluations. The additional sparsity percentages are configuration changes rather than new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V2 introduces Wanda+LoRA and Wanda+Full as evaluated retraining baselines in Tables 2–3, with training-data counts and sequence lengths matched to ELSA. These provide substantive controls absent from v1's comparisons. The original pruners and the relocated OWL/EvoPress comparison are retained.

E3.justification: V1 specifies batch size 8 and 4,096 steps universally. V2 instead reports 16/2,048 for OPT-125M and 32/1,024 for larger models at 50–60% sparsity, retaining 8/4,096 at 70–90%. Table 5 revises learning rates, penalties, and scheduling. V2 also introduces 95–99% configurations and inference/pruning timing protocols. These reported setting revisions do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Sections 5.2 and 5.5 add extreme-compression stress tests and a pruning-cost versus quality analysis, examining performance after baseline retraining and under tighter sparsity constraints. The original data-efficiency/objective and projection ablations remain unchanged, moving from Section 5.4 to Appendix C.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 reports mean inference latency but supplies no repetition count or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds efficiency, pruning-time, and retraining-comparison results; ELSA's new 99% sparsity result is 55.94/40.10 WikiText2/C4 perplexity. Tables 10–12 replace ELSA's 50–60% scores alongside revised settings, including LLaMA-2-7B's 50% average accuracy changing from 53.35 to 56.39. ELSA-L's reported memory reduction changes from 66% to 55%, now specifically referring to optimizer and auxiliary states. Existing 70–90% tabulated quality results are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, Assumptions 4.1–4.3, stationarity definition, convergence statements, and Appendix A proof are unchanged. Theorem 4.6 moves across a page boundary without a substantive revision.

C1.justification: V2 expands the headline empirical scope from approximately 80–90% sparsity to effectiveness at 95–99%. Its abstract, introduction, and discussion newly claim realized deployment benefits, including up to 3.98-fold throughput improvement and 7.80-fold memory compression. The central surrogate-free ADMM contribution remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations linking deployment gains to decoding dominated by sparse matrix-vector operations and arguing that ELSA converts pruning compute into quality more effectively. It also narrows the ELSA-L memory-saving statement to optimizer and auxiliary states. The original surrogate-objective explanation and memory discussion largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 substantially revises the hyperparameter specification, adds a model/sparsity-specific batch-and-step table, and explicitly states 32,768 training sequences of length 2,048. It documents matched-data baseline retraining, MACKO/RTX 3090 inference, and A100-80GB timing. Appendix B.1 changes environment/script availability from promised to stated available, although the PDFs cannot verify repository access.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to LoRA (Hu et al., 2022) and MACKO (Macko and Boža, 2025), and removes the bfloat16 reference by Kalamkar et al. The broader positioning against layer-wise surrogate-based pruning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: v1's main-text sections on other sparsity patterns and ablations become Appendix C.1–C.2, while the main text prioritizes extreme sparsity, deployment, and computational cost. The abstract, introduction, and discussion are revised around this emphasis; method and proof prose remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds dedicated inference-efficiency, extreme-sparsity, and compute-quality Tables 1–3, adds batch/step Table 6, and restructures hyperparameter Table 5. V1's Tables 1–3 become Tables 8, 7, and 9 in Appendix C, and Figure 6 moves there as well. This substantially redistributes the empirical displays while retaining the original plots.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked explicit matched-data pruning-plus-retraining controls and measured inference performance. V2 addresses these important gaps through Wanda retraining comparisons, pruning-cost measurements, and actual speed/memory benchmarks (Tables 1–3), substantially strengthening comparative validity and practical relevance. New benchmark details remain incomplete, and Section 5.5 incorrectly groups SparseGPT with perplexities of at least 10,000 despite Table 3 reporting 1430/864.5. These reporting weaknesses limit, but do not outweigh, the added validation.
